summary: Strong Bronze Age direction, with distinct occupational props and an excellent priest/trader hierarchy. The main weaknesses are modern-looking tunic construction, rigid stepped cloth and segmented long hems.
problems: The Field Tender's plain torso and rectangular short sleeves read too much like a modern T-shirt. The hoe's small rectangular head reads more like a mallet at this angle.
The Reed Weaver's diagonal garment reads as a staircase of rigid plates rather than one continuous fabric wrap.
The Water Carrier, Elder and High Priest have long garments that resolve into separate rectangular lower-leg panels, giving the hems a trouser-like appearance.
The Elder's flattened cap sits awkwardly against the exposed block hair, while the broad horizontal shoulder slab makes the shawl look stiff.
The Field Tender's hoe shaft disappears against the arm instead of showing a convincing hand grip. Prop clearance and articulated garment fit still need checking in walking poses.
fix: Water Carrier: Keep the jar, pad and asymmetric wool shoulder. Give the lower wrap a clear diagonal overlap and staggered hem; overlap the leg-following panels enough to conceal rectangular breaks without rigidly bridging the legs. Field Tender: Replace the T-shirt-like sleeves with a sleeveless wrapped tunic, add one broad overlapping front fold, and extend the sun cloth into a visible neck drape. Make the hoe blade a broad angled bronze plate, expose its face to the camera, and offset the shaft into the hand grip. Reed Weaver: Replace the three-step sash with a continuous diagonal cloth band connected over the shoulder and around the waist; retain the exposed shoulder and substantial reed bundle. Village Elder: Tuck or hide hair beneath a fuller wrapped headcloth. Replace the shoulder shelf with sloping torso panels and separate arm-following ends; retain the broad fringe and crooked stick. Rework the lower hem as overlapping cloth rather than two boxed legs. High Priest: Preserve the tiered crown, turquoise mantle, large sun pendant and tall sun staff. Refine only the segmented robe hem and verify staff clearance through the walk cycle. Caravan Leader: Preserve the red-and-lapis silhouette and contrasting woven borders. Slightly thicken the balance suspensions for stream readability and maintain a visible grip with both pans clear of the body.
